passage:
"Sahil, did you send Nani the voice note?" Keerthana asked.
"Yes, I sang the whole song."
"And you said 'Love you, Nani' at the end. She'll like that."
"But I made a mistake in the second line, so I sent it again."
"Nani won't mind. She likes hearing you."
"Will she show it to Aunty Lata? I sang in my funny voice."
Keerthana paused. "Ask her first. She can play it for herself, but you decide about others."
"Okay. Can I send a video of Bruno next?"
"Ask Nani if she wants it. And check that the dog isn't chewing your shoe." Sahil giggled. 🙂

qa.q: What did Sahil say at the end of the voice note?
qa.a: Sahil said, "Love you, Nani" at the end.

qa.q: Why was Sahil worried about the voice note being shared with Aunty Lata?
qa.a: Sahil sang in a funny voice and was afraid others might hear it, so wanted a say. Sahil seems to want to keep the fun for Nani only.

qa.q: What could Sahil do before sending a voice note or video to someone?
qa.a: Sahil could ask the person whether it is only for them, and think about whether it would feel okay if others heard it.

qa.q: How does Nani probably feel about hearing Sahil's voice?
qa.a: Nani probably feels warm and close to Sahil, because a voice carries warmth and tone in a way that a typed message doesn't.

grounding: A child sends voice notes and videos to family, showing warmth of voice and a reminder to think before sending because recordings can be forwarded.

passage: I'm Reena. Last winter I sent Yusuf a voice note from my grandmother's house. I was telling him about the snow and I said, "I miss you, you smell like a wet dog." I was joking. Yusuf sent back a heart and a laugh. But then my cousin heard it on his phone and told our whole class I had said Yusuf smells. I felt my stomach drop. Yusuf said it was okay, but I didn't record anything for a week. Now I think before I press send: would I be fine if other people hear it? Voice notes let people hear my smile, and I like that. 🙂

qa.q: What did Reena say in the voice note to Yusuf?
qa.a: Reena said, "I miss you, you smell like a wet dog," as a joke.

qa.q: What was Reena feeling when Reena's cousin told the class about the voice note?
qa.a: Reena's stomach dropped, which suggests worry and embarrassment. Reena may also have felt guilty that the joke reached people it was not meant for.

qa.q: What could Reena do next time she wants to send a personal voice note?
qa.a: Reena could ask whether it would be fine if others heard it, and keep jokes for people who understand the tone.

qa.q: How might Yusuf have felt about the voice note and its spread?
qa.a: Yusuf answered warmly with a heart and a laugh and said it was okay, but he may also have felt awkward about being talked about at school.

grounding: A child values how voice notes carry warmth and tone, and learns that recordings can be forwarded so it is worth thinking before sending.

passage:
Nani's notebook, Tuesday
Jasleen has started sending me voice notes every morning on her way to school. I hear the auto horn, her giggle, and "Good morning, Nani ji, I'm wearing the red clips you gave!" A typed message never makes me smile like this.
This evening she was recording something for her friend Parveen. She was copying a new girl's way of talking and laughing. Before she pressed send, I asked, "If that girl heard this, how would she feel? And can Parveen send it on?"
Jasleen stopped. "Anyone can forward it," she said slowly. She deleted it and recorded a different one, telling Parveen about the dance practice instead.
I told her I was proud she thought first.

qa.q: What does Jasleen say in her morning voice note to Nani?
qa.a: "Good morning, Nani ji, I'm wearing the red clips you gave!"

qa.q: What might Jasleen have been feeling when she said "Anyone can forward it"?
qa.a: She probably felt uneasy and a bit ashamed, realising the recording could be passed on and hurt the new girl.

qa.q: Which choice worked, and why?
qa.a: Nani asking questions instead of scolding worked, because Jasleen worked out the risk herself and chose a kinder message.

qa.q: How does Nani experience the morning voice notes?
qa.a: The voice notes make Nani feel close and happy, because she can hear warmth and small details a typed message would miss.

grounding: A caregiver's note shows a child sending warm voice notes and thinking before sending a recording that could be forwarded.

passage:
Friday night
Sabina moved to Guwahati last month and we're not allowed to call every day, so we send voice notes. Tonight she sent one singing our school song very badly, and I played it five times. Her voice made me feel like she was sitting on my bed.
I started a reply. I was going to tell her that Chhoden cried in class today after the test and everyone saw. Halfway through, I stopped. Sabina's cousin is in my class. What if Sabina plays it and her cousin hears? What if it gets forwarded?
I deleted it. Instead I recorded me and my little brother doing her song even worse. She sent back ten laughing faces.
- Pema

qa.q: How many times did Pema play Sabina's voice note?
qa.a: Five times.

qa.q: What made Pema stop halfway through the first reply?
qa.a: Pema felt worried that the voice note about Chhoden crying could be heard by Sabina's cousin or forwarded, which could embarrass Chhoden.

qa.q: What would you advise a child who wants to share news about someone else in a voice note?
qa.a: Pause and ask whether the person would be okay if it were forwarded; if not, share your own news instead.

qa.q: If you were Chhoden, what would you want Pema to do?
qa.a: You would want Pema to keep the crying private and not record it where others might hear.

grounding: A child sends warm voice notes to a friend and stops before recording something about another person that could be forwarded.

passage:
In the village near Kottayam, the new calf was born just after sunrise. Jomon ran with Appa's old phone to make a video for Kalyani Chechi, who worked in a hospital in the city.
"Chechi, look, she's standing! Her legs are like sticks!" he whispered, laughing.
Behind him Appa and the neighbour were arguing loudly about the fence. Jomon watched the clip back and heard every angry word. Chechi might show it to her friends, and they might send it on.
He walked to the far side of the shed, where only the hens were talking, and recorded again.
That night Chechi sent a voice note back. Her voice was soft and shaky. "Jomon, I miss home so much. Thank you for the calf."

qa.q: Where did Jomon go to record again?
qa.a: To the far side of the shed, where only the hens were talking.

qa.q: How did Kalyani Chechi seem to feel when she sent the voice note back?
qa.a: Her soft, shaky voice suggests she felt touched and homesick, missing the village and grateful for the calf video. 🥺

qa.q: What did Jomon do well before sending?
qa.a: He watched the clip back, noticed the argument could be forwarded, and chose to re-record in a quieter place.

qa.q: How might Appa feel if the first video had been sent?
qa.a: Appa might feel embarrassed if his argument about the fence was seen by strangers or passed around.

grounding: A child makes a warm video message and thinks before sending about whether recorded content could be forwarded.

passage: Every Sunday evening in Bergen, Ingrid recorded a voice note for her grandmother Beatriz in Lisbon. Typing in Portuguese was slow, but her voice could giggle, sing the rooster song, and say "saudades, Avó" in exactly the soft way Mamãe did. Avó always replied with a voice note that began with a long, happy sigh. On Monday, Ingrid's friend Sofie dared her to record an impression of their grumpy bus driver for the class chat. Ingrid held the microphone button down, then let go without sending anything. "What if someone forwards it and he hears it?" Sofie shrugged. Ingrid deleted it and recorded something else: the rooster song for Avó, a day early.

qa.q: What did Avó's replies always begin with?
qa.a: A long, happy sigh.

qa.q: Why did Ingrid let go of the button without sending?
qa.a: She felt uneasy, worried that a forwarded voice note could reach the bus driver and hurt him.

qa.q: What habit did Ingrid show that others could copy?
qa.a: Pausing before sending to ask who might hear it later, because a recording can travel far beyond the person it was made for.

qa.q: What might Avó Beatriz feel when she hears Ingrid's voice notes?
qa.a: Avó likely feels warm and close to her granddaughter, since the giggles and soft 'saudades' carry feeling that slow typed words cannot 🤍

grounding: It shows a child using voice notes to carry warmth to family, and stopping before sending a recording that could be forwarded and hurt someone.
